title: Wanted words are no compulsory payment

captions.physics: Asking through an ambiguous participation condition
captions.energy: Clarifying attention’s tie to required words
captions.emotions: Feeling dependence on a wanted confirmation

meaning: You can ask through an ambiguous condition of participation and clarify attention tied to a required phrase, acknowledging dependence on confirmation without making it compulsory payment for conversation.
text: On your Vishuddha, the Moon in the physical position can appear in a request through an ambiguous condition of participation. The Devil in energy supports readiness to clarify honestly a tie between attention and a required phrase. The Devil in emotions brings dependence on a wanted confirmation. Wanting to clarify a binding condition differs from strongly longing for the confirmation tied to it. You can recognise a phrase’s importance to your calm without making it the other person’s duty.

Suppose someone says, “If words are not too much trouble, say I am right”. It is unclear whether support after an argument or acceptance of the position itself is wanted. **Attention to a person is not paid for through compulsory confirmation**. You can name this link and discuss the actual question. Yet an exact “You are right” remains especially desirable, as though participation were otherwise unreal. This pull can be heard without declaring other words empty; explanation or willingness to listen can also contain an actual response.

Difficulty grows if every answer is still tested against the recognised condition: does it resemble the required formula enough? Understanding the tie has not yet changed listening. The constructive side of the Devil in energy helps notice this price again while preserving a genuine answer’s freedom. You can want confirmation without demanding it as proof of interest; strong desire requires neither immediate elimination nor treating disagreement as established evidence of absent attention.
